newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht, interbank rate steady in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht, interbank rate steady in late trade.

text.p: The Thai baht was steady in late quiet trade onshore on Tuesday, after being capped at the strong resistance level of around 30 baht per dollar, dealers said.
"The market was very quiet. The baht was traded at around 29.95-30.00 throughout the day," said one dealer at a European bank.
The baht was quoted at 29.95/29.97 to the dollar late onshore compared with 29.90/30.00 in early dealings.
The Bank of Thailand on Tuesday announced that the weighted average interbank exchange rate was 30.348 per dollar against 29.945 on Monday.
The reference rate is the average rate traded the previous day. It has been announced daily by the central bank since the baht was floated on July 2.
The dealer said the central bank has apparently tried to cap the baht/dollar trade at the 30.00 level, but no significant intervention by the central bank was seen on Tuesday.
The baht tumbled to a new record low of 30.80 in early Monday trade in the domestic market.
But the baht recovered significantly later after the Bank of Thailand intervened and issued a statement that it would take any necessary action to stabilise the currency.
In the offshore market, the baht was quoted at 29.70/29.90 late against 29.65/29.85 in early morning.
The baht/dollar one-month swap premium was at 28/33 satangs per dollar late in onshore market and 70/80 satangs in the offshore market.
The overnight interbank rate was steady at 18-20 percent, unchanged from early morning trade.
